# API Security Checklist: User Authentication and Authorization

**Purpose**: Review the completeness, clarity, and consistency of API authentication and security requirements  
**Created**: 2026-11-07  
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.  
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.  
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are the permitted self-service roles and the prohibition on administrator self-registration consistent across email and Google registration? [Consistency, Spec §FR-001, §FR-002, §FR-010]
- [ ] CHK002 Does the specification define who or what can lock an account, given that lock administration is out of scope? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK003 Are the required fields and identity-normalization rules clear for email registration and Google sign-in? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001, §FR-009, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 Are verification and recovery token lifetimes, one-time use, and invalidation requirements consistent across all user flows? [Consistency, Spec §FR-003, §FR-011, §FR-013]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is the expected user-facing behavior clear for invalid, expired, and already-used verification or reset links? [Clarity, Spec §FR-003, §FR-005, §FR-011, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK006 Is the account-linking rule unambiguous when a verified Google email matches an existing email/password account? [Clarity, Spec §FR-009, Clarifications]
- [ ] CHK007 Are the denial outcomes for unauthenticated users, wrong-role users, unverified users, and locked users distinguished clearly enough for clients? [Clarity, Spec §FR-007, §FR-014]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK008 Are authentication and authorization error response status and payload requirements defined for client handling? [Gap, Spec §FR-006–§FR-014]
- [ ] CHK009 Are measurable limits specified for login and recovery rate-limiting behavior? [Clarity, Spec §FR-015]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK010 Are concurrent registration and token-consumption outcomes defined sufficiently to prevent duplicate accounts or repeated token use? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK011 Are expected account and session outcomes described for email-provider and Google-provider outages? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 Is the interaction between password reset, logout, and all previously issued session credentials unambiguous? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, §FR-013, §SC-006]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK013 Are email-delivery and Google OAuth configuration responsibilities and failure expectations documented for deployment? [Dependency, Spec §Assumptions, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the boundary between authentication API scope and profile completion explicit for the account display name? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers.
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`.
